## What you will install, and why

| Tool | What it is | Why you need it |
|---|---|---|
| **Visual Studio Code** | A code editor and workspace | You write, run, and version-control your work in one window. |
| **Python and Jupyter extensions** | Add-ons for Visual Studio Code | Let Visual Studio Code run Python files and notebooks. |
| **Git** | Version-control software on your computer | Records the history of your changes. |
| **GitHub account** | An online home for Git repositories | Stores and shares your work; runs automatic checks. |
| **Python** | The programming language and its interpreter | Runs your code. |
| **A course environment** | A separate "room" for this course's packages | Keeps this course's package versions from clashing with anything else. |

## Two ways to install Python

Pick **one** and stay with it.

| Track | Tool | Choose it if… |
|---|---|---|
| **Default** | **uv** | You are new to Python. One tool installs Python, creates the environment, and installs packages; the steps are almost identical on macOS and Windows. |
| **Alternative** | **conda** (via **Miniforge**) | You already use conda, or you will need non-Python software later. |

## Packages we start with

We deliberately start small and add packages as the course needs them.

| Package | Used for |
|---|---|
| `numpy` | Arrays, vectorized math, random numbers |
| `scipy` | Probability distributions, optimization, statistical tests |
| `matplotlib` | Plots |
| `ipykernel` | Lets notebooks run code in your course environment |
| `jupyterlab` | A browser-based notebook interface (optional alternative to Visual Studio Code) |

## What to submit

Three screenshots:

1. The output of the setup-check script (Python and package versions).
2. The parabola plot from your first notebook.
3. Your test repository on GitHub after your first push.

## If nothing works

Do not spend more than an hour stuck. Come to class anyway: you can work in **GitHub Codespaces**, a browser version of Visual Studio Code, while we fix your installation.
